title: Connector SDK Charter

use_cases.outcome: connect only after explicit permission and visible scope review
read an allowed resource through a brokered, auditable handle
diagnose health without exposing credentials or content
validate a connector against deterministic local contracts

audiences.needs: safe, understandable account and project capabilities
permission review, disable, revoke, and support visibility
health, diagnostics, incident containment, and audit evidence
typed contracts, mocks, diagnostics, and fail-closed tests

boundaries.rule: undeclared capabilities and destinations are denied
connectors never receive plaintext secrets or tokens
boundaries.enforcement: opaque secret references and redacted diagnostics

boundaries.rule: novel, character, project, and account data stay separately scoped
boundaries.enforcement: brokered handles, consent, and audit records

boundaries.rule: network access is limited to declared destinations and protocols
connectors use approved Account Center slots, not arbitrary layout injection
boundaries.enforcement: typed extension points and visual regression coverage

boundaries.rule: certification, provider exposure, publication, and release stay gated
boundaries.enforcement: separate evidence and operator approval gates

non_goals.reason: requires external review, publication, and support evidence

non_goals.statement: run arbitrary third-party code in the desktop process
expose passwords, tokens, or API keys to connectors or logs
non_goals.reason: the security contract requires opaque references and redaction

non_goals.statement: collect connector or writing telemetry without consent
non_goals.reason: privacy and consent are explicit product boundaries

non_goals.statement: certify a new provider from the charter alone
non_goals.reason: certification requires its own live or otherwise authorized evidence

non_goals.statement: publish or release an SDK package from this local contract
non_goals.reason: release authorization, signing, and external gates are separate

exit_criteria.description: Each supported use case names one capability and outcome.
exit_criteria.evidence: canonical charter manifest and evaluator report

exit_criteria.description: Each audience has a role and a concrete product need.
exit_criteria.evidence: canonical audience list in the charter manifest

exit_criteria.description: Security, data, runtime, UI, and release boundaries name enforcement.
Unsafe or externally gated work is explicitly excluded.
exit_criteria.evidence: canonical non-goal list in the charter manifest

exit_criteria.description: Every success metric has a target, measurement, and source.
exit_criteria.evidence: metric definitions and focused evaluator tests

exit_criteria.description: Certification, provider exposure, publication, and release remain separate gates.
exit_criteria.evidence: claim boundary and external gate record

claim_boundary: This local record defines the Connector SDK charter; it does not install, execute, certify, expose, release, or publish a connector.
Permission defaults, opaque secrets, scoped data, declared network access, approved UI slots, and separate release gates are contract boundaries, not live provider observations.
Certification, provider exposure, external telemetry, signing, publication, and release remain DEFERRED-EXTERNAL.
The authorized GitHub certification example does not authorize claims for other providers or bypass the later trust, manifest, runtime, and release gates.
